title: Setting and Owning the Frame
hook: A circulation map can stop a design meeting from becoming a price hunt.
counterintuition: Frame control is not louder confidence, but calmer interpretation control. The room may seem to be judging facts while it is actually judging the frame those facts have been placed inside.
tryThisNow: Write the weak label the room may put on your offer. Beside it, write the decision frame you want judged before any detail appears.
keyTakeaway: Own the frame by naming the real decision calmly and early, so the room judges your facts inside the right interpretation instead of a weaker inherited assumption.

breakdown.fastRead:
Clara unrolls a map under a marble paperweight. A trustee calls the library plan decorative before the public access count appears.

She can defend every line item, or she can reset the frame. She slides the map forward and names the choice: public access versus storage, not style.

That is frame control. A live pitch is shaped by rival meanings. If the room decides you are selling decoration, your budget facts will sound decorative too.
breakdown.deepRead:
Patrick advises a pro cycling team on recovery protocols. The coach gives a toughness speech, and everyone knows the frame: rest is softness. Patrick waits until the speech ends. Then he places the power-output decline chart beside the race calendar.

"I am not protecting comfort," he says. "I am protecting watts in September."

The facts did not change. The interpretation did.

Frame control works because status, momentum, and assumptions arrive before content. A room can turn a renovation into cost trimming, recovery into indulgence, feed pellets into price per ton, or legal aid into charity spending. Once that frame is active, every fact you offer is bent toward it. React too fast and you confirm their terms. Overexplain and you sound trapped inside them. Accept the assumption and the pitch shrinks.

The move is not aggression. The move is calm ownership of what kind of decision is being made.

If Patrick had answered with a longer medical lecture, the coach could have kept the softness frame alive. By using the race calendar and watts, he changes the meaning before adding detail. The room is still free to disagree, but it now has to disagree with a performance claim instead of a comfort claim.
breakdown.fullRead:
Three salmon feed pellets sit on a white sample tray. Erik has a harvest-week table ready, but the farm operator asks only for price per ton. The question sounds practical. It is also a frame. If Erik answers inside it, the cheaper pellet wins before growth rate has a chance to matter.

He turns the tray toward the growth table. "Which number controls harvest week?" he asks. Now the room is not choosing feed as a commodity. It is choosing the biology that determines the season. Price still matters, but it no longer gets to be the only meaning in the room.

Frame control is the first move because every later move depends on the frame. Story lands differently when you are treated as a peer instead of a vendor. Intrigue lands differently when the room accepts that the decision has consequence. Prize lands differently when value has not been reduced to begging. Decision lands differently when the room has not already defined you as someone asking for a favor.

Ask yourself a blunt question: what weak interpretation could the room use before you speak?

Kathryn, an airport retail operator, sees her local-food concession bid being boxed into rent per square foot. Before, she answered rent with rent and lost the larger point. After, she clips receipt timestamps beside the gate-delay report and points to dwell time from delayed flights. The lease scoring rubric is still there, but the frame shifts from rent alone to passenger value during delay.

Beth, a legal aid director, misses the frame once and marks it later on a yellow legal pad beside eviction notices. She accepted charity spending, then tried to make the charity sound efficient. The better frame was avoidable county cost: families without representation become shelter, school disruption, and emergency spending. In the margin, she writes the replacement frame before rewriting any numbers.

The caution is simple. Do not confuse frame control with dominance theater. You are not trying to humiliate the room, act above it, or refuse reasonable questions. You are making sure the question is the right question. A calm reframe gives everyone a better decision surface.

Lucia, a premium coffee importer, faces a grocery buyer comparing her origin-lot beans to discount bulk bags. The burlap sample bag sits beside a stained cupping ledger. She stops answering the discount comparison and asks whether the buyer wants a commodity shelf or a destination shelf. Only then does she open the ledger. The beans have not changed. The shelf has.

The frame bends the facts toward the active interpretation. Set it before the facts are asked to carry weight.

The same discipline applies when the frame arrives politely. A buyer may not sound hostile when she says, "Let's compare this on price." A committee may not sound dismissive when it calls a public access plan decorative. The danger is that polite frames feel normal, so you answer them before asking whether they name the real decision. A steady presenter hears the hidden category first. Then the facts can work inside the right category.

examples.title: Harriet Slides the Circulation Map Forward

planSpec.domain: architect presenting a library renovation concept to preservation trustees
planSpec.audience: a design lead being treated as a vendor who must defend every line item
planSpec.stakes: the trustees reduce the project to cost cuts before hearing the civic-use frame
planSpec.requiredBeat: when a trustee calls the design decorative, she pauses, slides the circulation map forward, and names the decision as public access versus storage, not style preference

examples.scenario: Harriet slides a vellum circulation map from under a marble paperweight beside the preservation rulebook. "This feels decorative," a trustee says before she reaches the public access count. Her pen stops above the budget line. She must decide whether to defend trim costs or slide the map forward and name the choice as public access versus storage. Harriet keeps the map in front of the trustee, so the next fact has to answer public use rather than decorative taste.
examples.whatToDo: Pause and move the circulation map to the center. Reframe the decision around public access before discussing line items or style.
examples.whyItMatters: The trustees are judging decoration. If Clara accepts that frame, every budget fact sounds optional. Public access gives the facts a stronger meaning.

examples.title: Patrick Reframes Recovery as Watts

planSpec.domain: sports medicine specialist advising a pro cycling team on recovery protocols
planSpec.audience: a clinician facing coaches who frame recovery as softness
planSpec.stakes: riders keep losing late-season power because the staff treats rest as indulgence
planSpec.requiredBeat: he lets the coach finish the toughness speech, then places the power-output decline chart beside the race calendar and reframes recovery as preserving watts

examples.scenario: Patrick sets the laminated race calendar beside his crankset power report in the team bus. The coach finishes a speech about toughness while the recovery protocol sheet waits in Patrick's folder. He has to choose whether to argue about rest or place the power-output decline chart beside September races and reframe recovery as preserving watts. Patrick points to the race calendar instead of the brochure margin, so the coach has to answer the performance category he just named.
examples.whatToDo: Let the speech end, then connect recovery to late-season power. Use the race calendar and decline chart to change the frame from softness to output.
examples.whyItMatters: Arguing about toughness keeps Patrick inside the coach's frame. Watts give the room a performance frame where recovery can be judged seriously.

examples.title: Erik Turns the Feed Tray Toward Harvest

planSpec.domain: aquaculture feed supplier pitching a new pellet blend to salmon farm operators
planSpec.audience: a supplier whose offer is being framed as a commodity price quote
planSpec.stakes: the farm chooses the cheaper pellet and absorbs slower growth for an entire season
planSpec.requiredBeat: when the operator asks only for price per ton, the supplier turns the feed sample tray toward the growth table and asks which number controls harvest week

examples.scenario: Erik lines three feed pellets on a white sample tray beside his harvest-week table. The operator taps the price-per-ton sheet and asks for the discount. Erik's hand hovers over the price column. He must decide whether to answer inside the commodity frame or turn the tray toward the growth table and ask which number controls harvest week. Erik turns the pellets toward the harvest table, forcing the buyer to judge growth timing instead of chasing a commodity discount.
examples.whatToDo: Move from price per ton to harvest timing. Put the feed sample tray next to the growth table and make the operator judge the season, not only the invoice.
examples.whyItMatters: A price-only frame makes the cheaper pellet look responsible. Harvest timing restores the real cost of slow growth to the decision.

examples.title: Kathryn Points to Delayed-Flight Receipts

planSpec.domain: airport retail operator defending a local-food concession bid
planSpec.audience: an operator being boxed into rent-per-square-foot comparison
planSpec.stakes: the airport loses a distinctive tenant mix and the operator loses a ten-year lease
planSpec.requiredBeat: she changes the conversation from rent alone to dwell time by pointing to receipt timestamps from delayed flights

examples.scenario: Kathryn spreads receipt timestamps across a gate-delay report in the concession office after the airport lease interview. Before, she answered rent per square foot with a better rent number and watched the committee box her local-food bid into rent alone. Now she points to delayed-flight purchase times and changes the frame to passenger dwell-time value. Kathryn leaves the timestamps beside the lease sheet, so the committee has to price missed buying moments rather than square footage alone.
examples.whatToDo: Use the delay report and timestamps before debating rent. Make passenger dwell time the decision frame, then show how the bid fits the lease rubric.
examples.whyItMatters: Rent alone flattens the bid into a commodity. Dwell time connects tenant mix to airport revenue and passenger experience.

examples.title: Beth Rewrites the County Cost Frame

planSpec.domain: legal aid director asking county supervisors for eviction-defense funding
planSpec.audience: a nonprofit leader facing a room that frames the request as charity spending
planSpec.stakes: families lose representation while county shelter costs rises
planSpec.requiredBeat: she marks the point where she accepted the charity frame and writes the replacement frame, avoidable county cost, in the margin

examples.scenario: Beth sets a yellow legal pad beside her stack of eviction notices and shelter cost table. After the county budget meeting, she finds the point where she accepted the charity frame and tried to sound efficient. In the margin, beside the budget note, she writes the replacement frame: avoidable county cost. Beth turns the shelter table toward the finance chair, moving the choice from goodwill to money the county is already spending.
examples.whatToDo: Open the next request with avoidable county cost, then show eviction notices and shelter costs as connected budget facts instead of charity evidence.
examples.whyItMatters: Charity spending makes supervisors ask how little they can give. Avoidable cost makes them judge whether inaction is already expensive.

examples.title: Lucia Asks About the Shelf

planSpec.domain: premium coffee importer negotiating with a grocery chain buyer
planSpec.audience: an importer whose beans are being compared to discount bulk bags
planSpec.stakes: the chain strips the origin story and forces a price-only listing
planSpec.requiredBeat: she stops answering the discount comparison and asks whether the buyer wants a commodity shelf or a destination shelf before opening the cupping ledger

examples.scenario: Near the buyer's category desk at 8:30 a.m., Lucia sets a burlap coffee sample bag beside a stained cupping ledger, a shelf photo, and an origin lot code. The buyer compares her beans to discount bulk bags for the third time. Lucia must decide whether to defend price again or ask whether the chain wants a commodity shelf or a destination shelf. Lucia keeps the shelf photo beside the beans, changing the question from cheaper pounds to the kind of aisle the chain wants to own.
examples.whatToDo: Ask the shelf question before the price answer. Then use the cupping ledger and origin lot code to support the destination frame.
examples.whyItMatters: The discount comparison strips the beans of meaning. The shelf frame lets the buyer judge whether the product is meant to create a different kind of aisle.

questions.prompt: An architect hears trustees call a public library redesign decorative before seeing circulation data. What should she recognize first?
choices: A frame collision: the room is judging style while she needs it to judge access.
A need for more beautiful renderings.
A sign that preservation trustees dislike public use.
questions.explanation: The issue is the room's interpretation. Renderings or assumptions about trustees miss the active frame: decoration versus access.

questions.prompt: In the team bus after a mountain stage, the cycling coach calls recovery soft while the power chart is still folded. A cycling coach frames recovery as softness. Which reply best owns the frame without disrespect?
choices: Tell the coach toughness is outdated.
Place power decline beside the race calendar and name recovery as preserving watts.
Skip the coach and speak only to riders.
questions.explanation: Watts preserve the performance frame the coach respects while changing the meaning of recovery. Insults or bypassing the coach create status noise.

questions.prompt: At a salmon farm procurement table, the operator taps the price sheet while the harvest-week table sits beside the feed tray. A salmon farm asks only for price per ton on a feed blend. What move best avoids losing frame?
choices: Match the cheaper competitor's price.
Read the full ingredient list.
Ask which number controls harvest week and connect pellets to growth timing.
questions.explanation: Harvest timing reframes the decision around season value. Price matching accepts the commodity frame, and ingredients can still sound like commodity detail.

questions.prompt: During an airport lease interview, the committee keeps returning to rent per square foot while gate-delay receipts sit in the packet. An airport lease committee boxes a local-food bid into rent per square foot. What is the strongest analysis?
choices: The operator should shift the frame to passenger dwell-time value before arguing rent.
The operator should avoid rent entirely because it weakens local identity.
The operator should add more menu photography.
questions.explanation: Dwell time changes the decision surface while still allowing rent to matter. Avoiding rent or adding photos fails to answer the active scoring frame.

questions.prompt: A legal aid director realizes she accepted the charity-spending frame in a county budget meeting. What replacement frame fits best?
choices: The moral duty of public officials.
Avoidable county cost from eviction fallout.
The personal courage of tenants.
questions.explanation: Avoidable cost meets supervisors inside budget responsibility. Moral duty and tenant stories may matter, but they can keep the request outside the budget frame.

questions.prompt: At a grocery chain buying desk, the importer hears her origin-lot beans compared to discount bulk bags for the third time. A coffee importer keeps defending her bean price against discount bulk bags. Which question best resets the frame?
choices: Can you pay a little more for quality?
Do you understand origin lots?
Do you want a commodity shelf or a destination shelf?
questions.explanation: The shelf question changes what the buyer is judging. The other options sound defensive and keep price or buyer competence at the center.

questions.prompt: In a tense review meeting, a presenter hears an unfair assumption and feels the urge to answer every possible objection at once. A presenter reacts instantly to an unfair assumption and starts explaining every detail. What risk does that create?
choices: The explanation can confirm the weaker frame by sounding trapped inside it.
The room will always appreciate the extra transparency.
The presenter will accidentally create too much status.
questions.explanation: Fast overexplaining often accepts the other side's terms. The better move is to pause and reset what kind of decision is being made.

questions.prompt: During sales training, a team lead claims the only way to own frame is to act superior to the buyer. A sales lead says frame control means acting superior so the room feels lower status. How should you evaluate that?
choices: Correct, because status is the only thing that matters.
Wrong, because practical frame control calmly sets interpretation without disrespect.
Correct only when the buyer starts aggressively.
questions.explanation: Disrespect is theater, not control. The useful move is to make sure facts are judged inside the right decision frame.

questions.prompt: A buyer frames a software rollout as another tool to manage. The seller needs it judged as a risk-control system. What should happen before feature detail?
choices: A calm reframe of the decision from tool adoption to risk control.
A complete feature list to prove the buyer is wrong.
A discount that makes the tool easier to approve.
questions.explanation: The reframe changes how features will be heard. A feature dump and discount both accept the weaker interpretation.

reviewCards.front: A trustee calls your access plan decorative before seeing usage counts. What is the frame collision?
reviewCards.back: It is the moment the room is judging your offer through one interpretation while you need it judged through another. Catch it before arguing details.

reviewCards.front: A room treats your offer as a commodity. What should you do before defending quality?
reviewCards.back: Reset the decision frame. Show what the room is really choosing, such as timing, access, risk, or value, before comparing features.

reviewCards.front: Why can overexplaining weaken frame control?
reviewCards.back: It can make you sound trapped inside the other side's assumptions. A pause and a clean reframe often carry more status than a defensive proof pile.

reviewCards.front: A senior buyer tries to win status by mocking your price. How is frame control different from dominance theater?
reviewCards.back: Frame control clarifies what kind of decision is being made. Dominance theater tries to win status by disrespecting the room, which usually creates resistance.

reviewCards.front: A buyer has accepted your stronger frame. What should happen before the facts do heavy work?
reviewCards.back: After the right frame is active. Facts bend toward the interpretation already in the room, so set that interpretation first.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: You learn to notice the room's hidden interpretation before your facts are judged. The skill is calm reframing, not force.

ifThenPlans.plan: If the room frames your request as cost, then name the operational risk or avoided loss before defending the amount.
If a buyer compares you to the cheapest option, then ask what outcome the category is supposed to produce before discussing price.
If someone reduces your work to a preference, then move the evidence that shows the real decision to the center of the table.
If leaders ask a question that shrinks the issue, then answer briefly and restate the larger decision frame before adding details.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Write one weak frame a listener could put on your offer, then write one sentence that calmly replaces it with the decision you want judged.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Before each important meeting, list the default frame the room may use. Afterward, note whether you accepted it, fought it, or replaced it.

memorableLines.text: The facts did not change. The interpretation did.
memorableLines.why: It makes the frame shift visible without inflating the idea.

memorableLines.text: The frame bends the facts toward the active interpretation.
memorableLines.why: It gives the reader a memorable rule for why order and interpretation matter.

memorableLines.text: A calm reframe gives everyone a better decision surface.
memorableLines.why: It separates practical control from status theatrics.
